title: Staying safe online: passwords
examples: How many characters should a strong password have?
What is the difference between a password and a passphrase?
Is it okay to write my passwords down somewhere?

explain.say: Today we are learning about keeping your accounts safe online. A strong password is your first line of defence.

items: Mix types: use letters, numbers, symbols
Avoid personal info: no names or birthdays

explain.say: A simple password like your pet's name is very easy to guess. Try mixing capital letters and small letters.
Password managers are special apps that remember complex passwords for you. You only need to remember one master password.
Two-factor login adds a second check when you log in. This could be a code sent to your phone.
In real life, think about your house keys and a secret code. The key is the password, and the code is the second factor.
A common mistake is reusing the same password everywhere. If one site gets hacked, all your accounts are at risk.

items: Never use the same password twice
If one site leaks, others are safe
Use unique passwords for every account

faq.q: Do I need to change my password often?
faq.a: It is good practice to change your password if you suspect it has been seen by someone else. You can also change it if a service updates its security rules.
asks: How often should I change my password?

faq.q: Are there any characters I should never use in a password?
faq.a: You should avoid using characters that are easily guessed, like '123' or 'qwerty'. Also, avoid using common dictionary words.
asks: What characters are bad for passwords?

faq.q: If I forget my password, can a password manager help?
faq.a: Yes, if you remember your master password, the manager can help you access all your other saved passwords. This is why remembering that one master password is important.
asks: How does a manager help with forgotten passwords?

faq.a: It is highly recommended to use two-factor login for important accounts like email. It adds a significant layer of protection even if your password is stolen.
asks: What is the benefit of two-factor login?

faq.q: Are passphrases better than complex passwords?
faq.a: Passphrases, which are short sentences, are often easier to remember and can be very strong. They combine length with random words.
asks: Are long sentences okay for passwords?

facts: A strong password should be long and contain a mix of character types.
Password managers store and generate complex, unique passwords for many accounts.
Two-factor authentication requires a second piece of proof besides your password.
Never share your password or your two-factor code with anyone.

quiz.say: Which combination is the strongest password?
quiz.show: A) cat123 B) Password! C) C@tP@sswOrd7
quiz.why: This option uses capital letters, small letters, numbers, and symbols, making it very hard to guess.

wrong.1: This is too short and only uses lowercase letters and numbers.
wrong.2: This is a common word that people often guess or see in movies.
wrong.3: Using a pet's name makes it predictable to people who know you.

quiz.say: What is the main benefit of using a password manager?
quiz.show: A) It guesses your passwords B) It remembers them for you C) It changes your passwords

options.show: B) It remembers them for you
options.say: B) It remembers them for you

options.show: D) It tells you if a password is weak
options.say: D) It tells you if a password is weak

quiz.why: The manager securely stores all your unique passwords so you only need to remember one master key.

wrong.1: Password managers do not guess; they store what you create.
wrong.2: While it helps you create new ones, its main job is storage, not active changing.
wrong.3: Some managers do this, but its core function is secure storage, not just checking strength.

quiz.say: If a website requires a second code sent to your phone, what security feature are you using?
quiz.why: This process requires two different types of proof, making it much safer than just a password.

wrong.0: A unique password only means it is different from others, not that it requires a second step.
wrong.2: Password strength only relates to the complexity of the password itself.
wrong.3: A manager helps you store the password, but it is not the second step.
